text:
I read all 9 tracked files. This is a small Next.js App Router site, and `geo.config.json` sets the policy: allow AI search crawlers, block training crawlers. I audited against that policy. I didn't build or run the site.

## Problems, most important first

**1. The training-crawler block is incomplete, so it doesn't match `geo.config.json:8`.**
`public/robots.txt:5-9` blocks only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot`. Other training crawlers fall under `User-agent: *` (line 1) and are allowed. Add a `Disallow: /` group for each of these:
- `Google-Extended`
- `Applebot-Extended`
- `CCBot`
- `Bytespider`
- `meta-externalagent`
- `anthropic-ai`
- `cohere-ai`

`Google-Extended` and `Applebot-Extended` don't affect search ranking or indexing.

**2. The AI search crawlers are allowed only implicitly.**
`geo.config.json:7` says `allow`, but `robots.txt` never names them. They get in through the `*` group (lines 1-3), which also carries `Disallow: /account`. A bot-specific group replaces the `*` group, so if someone later adds a group for one of these bots, that bot loses the `/account` rule unless it's repeated. Add explicit groups for `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`, `Claude-User` and `Applebot`. Each group should have `Allow: /` and `Disallow: /account`.

**3. There is no structured data anywhere.**
None of `app/layout.tsx:1-13`, `app/page.tsx:4` or `app/visit/page.tsx:4` has any JSON-LD. Add:
- `Organization` or `LocalBusiness` to the layout or home page, with name, URL and founding date (1952).
- `LocalBusiness` or `Place` on the visit page, with address, geo and `openingHoursSpecification` (Thu–Sun, Apr–Oct).
- `BreadcrumbList` on the inner pages.

**4. The page content is too thin to be cited.**
- **`app/visit/page.tsx:1,4`:** The description promises "directions", but the page has no address, postcode, map link, parking or phone number.
- **`app/varieties/page.tsx:4`:** It says "over forty varieties" but lists only two. Give each variety its own entry or page, with name, flavour, use and picking season.
- **`app/page.tsx:4`:** It is one sentence. Add what you sell, how to buy, and the Herefordshire location.

Concrete facts in plain HTML (lists, headings, a table) are what AI answers quote.

**5. Nothing sets site-wide metadata defaults.**
`app/layout.tsx:1` sets only `metadataBase`. Add:
- A `title.template` and a default title and description.
- `openGraph` (title, description, image, `siteName`, `locale`) and `twitter` cards.
- Per-page `openGraph`, which is also missing from `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1` and `app/visit/page.tsx:1`.

Without these, shared links and previews have no image or title.

**6. `/account` is both disallowed and noindexed, which conflict.**
`public/robots.txt:3` blocks crawling, and `app/account/page.tsx:1` sets `noindex`. Crawlers can't fetch the page, so they never see the `noindex`. If someone links to the URL, it can still appear in results as a bare URL. The page isn't in the sitemap, so the risk is low. Pick one: drop the `Disallow` and keep `noindex`, or keep the `Disallow` and accept the small risk. The page also has no `description`.

**7. The sitemap has no `lastmod`.**
`public/sitemap.xml:3-5` lists the three URLs without `<lastmod>`. It's also hand-maintained, so new pages won't be added automatically. Generate it with `app/sitemap.ts` and real modification dates.

**8. Smaller issues**
- **`app/layout.tsx:7`:** Plain `<a>` tags cause full page loads. Use `next/link`. The `<nav>` needs `aria-label`, and it needs a `<header>` and `<footer>` around the shell.
- **`app/page.tsx:1`:** The title is "Orchard: heritage apple trees", which doesn't say where. Consider adding "Herefordshire".
- **`app/layout.tsx:9`:** `data-nosnippet` on the cookie notice is fine. Just don't spread it to real content.
- **Optional:** Add `llms.txt` with a short site summary and key URLs. Support for it is inconsistent.

## What's already fine
- `lang="en"` is set (`app/layout.tsx:4`).
- Every indexable page has a unique title, description and canonical URL.
- Each page has one `h1`.
- The sitemap is referenced from `robots.txt` (line 11) and its URLs match the canonicals.

I haven't changed anything. I can implement fixes 1–5 and 7 if you want.
